features.summary: Recent updates to WebRender, the GPU compositor in Firefox, focus on enhancing the precision and efficiency of rendering elements on the web. Notably, changes like **snapping transformed border thickness to whole device pixels** improve the clarity of borders and shadows, ensuring they align correctly with the pixel grid for crisp visuals. Adjustments to rendering text and box shadows under various transformations further enhance the visual quality, especially during animations. The updates also involve some cleanup, removing unused code paths and simplifying how pictures are prepared, which can lead to better performance and lower resource usage while browsing. Overall, these changes aim to create a smoother, more visually appealing web experience for users.

features.summary: Recent updates to the 2D graphics component of Firefox have focused on improving text rendering efficiency and accuracy. By tightening various processes, such as limiting the number of components assigned during glyph shaping and ensuring that incomplete glyph data is cleared if the shaping process fails, Firefox aims to deliver more reliable rendering of text. Additionally, optimizations were made to the caching of shaped words, employing a modified hash method to enhance performance. These changes not only streamline text processing but also lead to an overall **improvement in how clear and accurate text appears** on the screen, which is essential for user experience in web applications.

features.summary: Recent updates in the **compositing and layers** area of Firefox enhance the way scroll events are handled and improve performance when rendering graphics. Notably, the browser now _eagerly_ snapshots the scroll state through ScrollTimeline, which allows for more responsive interactions and smoother animations during scrolling. Additionally, a new preference has been added to adjust autoscroll speed, tailoring the experience to individual users. Improvements to how the browser manages and synchronizes visual and layout scroll offsets help ensure a seamless browsing experience, particularly when navigating content that involves complex layering or rendering techniques. These changes collectively aim to make scrolling more efficient and visually appealing for users.

This includes the removal of outdated checks related to the context's status, helping to streamline the performance of WebGL. Additionally, there are updates to support Metal ANGLE, which enhances graphics processing on macOS devices, ensuring better rendering and compatibility. Other improvements involve updating coding standards and removing deprecated configurations, contributing to a cleaner and more efficient codebase. **These enhancements will lead to a smoother graphics experience for users, especially when running complex visual applications or games online.**
